title: Recursion vs Iteration Check
description: Compare stack cost and when to prefer loops.

questions.prompt: Calling a naive recursive factorial with `n = 100_000` in JavaScript typically:

options.text: Risks `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`
Is converted to a `for` loop automatically

questions.explanation: Deep recursion stores unfinished work on the call stack and can throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`.

options.text: Do not reliably optimize tail calls — prefer iteration for deep linear depth

questions.explanation: JS engines do not reliably optimize tail calls — write iterative code if depth is linear in `n`.

options.text: When structure is hierarchical (e.g. tree walks)
Only when you must avoid any stack

questions.explanation: Recursion often matches hierarchical structure (trees, divide-and-conquer). Prefer iteration when depth can be huge.

questions.prompt: An iterative tree walk with an explicit `stack = []` compared to recursion:

options.text: Uses a completely different asymptotic space idea
Uses the same space idea, stored in a different place

questions.explanation: A tree walk’s iterative version needs an explicit stack — same space idea, different place. Convert by identifying state each frame holds.
